signals.name: CoreWeave, Inc.
signals.label: Credit markets won't believe the equity rally
signals.detail: CoreWeave's 9.75% 2031 bond yield hit 15.78% and its five-year CDS spread blew out above 1,140bps this week even as the stock bounced roughly 7.35% intraday on Oct 19, 2026 alongside a broader AI-stock recovery (Goldman Sachs upgraded it to Buy). Evercore ISI's trading desk said credit markets are effectively saying "no mas" to AI debt without operating cash-flow support, a view sharply at odds with retail sentiment, which AltIndex still puts at 57.6% positive on X/Twitter (1,828 mentions). CoreWeave has taken on more than $51bn of debt/obligations to fund its AI buildout.
signals.takeaway: When CDS spreads say distressed and retail sentiment says buy the dip, trust the credit market first.

signals.name: Oracle Corporation
signals.label: Congress keeps buying what credit markets are selling
signals.detail: Oracle's five-year CDS spread widened to ~288-315bps -- a record, roughly 3x a year prior -- and shares fell as much as 9% on Oct 14-15, 2026 as the investment-grade hyperscaler became the bellwether for AI-debt contagion spilling over from CoreWeave. Yet CapitolTrades/AltIndex data shows Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) disclosed Oracle purchases in the $1,001-$50,000 range across multiple filings between May and August 2026, buying into the same debt-funded AI-capex story credit markets are now pricing as risky.
signals.takeaway: A congressional buyer and a blown-out CDS market can't both be right about Oracle's AI-debt risk.

signals.name: MP Materials Corp.

signals.detail: MP Materials CEO James Litinsky has sold 1,185,167 shares for an estimated $77.87 million across 18 separate sales in the trailing 12 months, part of $144.92M in total insider selling against just $1.51M in insider buying (MarketBeat/Fintel, mid-October 2026). signals.takeaway: Heavy insider selling into a political tailwind is a caution flag on MP's run, even if the thematic story stays intact.

signals.name: Lynas Rare Earths Ltd
signals.label: Lynas bets ~A$968m that the West needs its own heavy rare earths
signals.detail: Lynas agreed in mid-October 2026 to acquire Meteoric Resources for approximately A$968 million to gain Meteoric's Caldeira ionic-clay heavy rare earths project in Brazil, lifting pro forma measured-and-indicated TREO resources by 79% and ore reserves by 26%. The move follows Lynas becoming the first supplier of dysprosium/terbium outside China (FY2026 revenue +76% y/y to AUD 977.95M). Timing is pointed: China's one-year pause on its Oct-2025 rare-earth export controls lapses Nov 10, 2026, with no extension published as of Oct 16.
signals.takeaway: Lynas is moving aggressively to lock in non-China heavy rare-earth supply right as the China export-pause deadline looms -- the clearest fundamental signal on the watchlist.
